findings.title: Shutdown flag causes queued items to be dropped
findings.body: FixedQueuePool.shutdown sets worker.shutdown=True before draining, and OrderedQueueWorker.run checks `while not self.shutdown` at the top of the loop. A worker that has just finished one item will exit on the next iteration even if many items remain in its queue. q.shutdown(immediate=False) is meant to drain, but the flag defeats it. Consequence is silent loss of results that were already accepted and tracked in OffsetTracker, they will never be processed nor committed.

findings.title: Single shared queue_pool used by multiple partition strategies
findings.body: ResultsStrategyFactory creates one FixedQueuePool in __init__ but create_thread_queue_parallel_worker creates a new SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy per partition assignment sharing that same pool, offset_tracker, and queues, each with its own commit_thread and commit closure. Concurrent commit loops race on get_committable/mark_committed, and close/terminate of one strategy shuts down the pool still in use by other partitions. Consequence is double commits, missed commits, and premature worker shutdown on rebalance.

findings.title: join() destroys processing state instead of flushing
findings.body: SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.join calls close(), which stops the commit thread and shuts down all queue workers. In Arroyo join(timeout) is expected to block until in-flight work is done without tearing down the strategy, and may be called repeatedly. Consequence is that a poll/join cycle or rebalance can permanently kill the shared pool and lose queued work.

findings.title: wait_until_empty ignores in-flight work
findings.body: FixedQueuePool.wait_until_empty and get_stats use only Queue.qsize(), which drops to zero as soon as a worker has dequeued an item, before result_processor finishes and before OffsetTracker.complete_offset. Callers checking total_items==0 conclude processing is done while work is still running. Consequence is flaky tests and premature commit/shutdown decisions in production code that polls queue depth.

findings.title: Partition lock creation is racy and leaks state
findings.body: OffsetTracker._get_partition_lock does get then setdefault on plain dict partition_locks without any global lock. Concurrent add/complete from many workers can create multiple Lock objects and mutate all_offsets/outstanding/last_committed dicts concurrently. In CPython this can return different locks to different threads, breaking the per-partition mutual exclusion that get_committable_offsets relies on. Consequence is corrupted offset sets and unsafe commits.

findings.title: Commit scan iterates full offset range
findings.body: OffsetTracker.get_committable_offsets computes min/max of all_offsets then loops `for offset in range(start, max_offset+1)`. If there is any gap the loop cost is proportional to the offset distance, not the number of tracked messages. A large skipped offset or long backlog makes the 1-second commit loop scan hundreds of thousands of integers per partition while holding the partition lock. Consequence is commit-thread stalls and blocked add/complete.

findings.title: FilteredPayload triggers exception log path on every skip
findings.body: SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit calls decoder unconditionally, but the real decoder ResultsStrategyFactory.decode_payload asserts `not isinstance(payload, FilteredPayload)` and raises AssertionError for filtered messages. The strategy relies on the outer except to then add+complete the offset, logging an exception stack for normal operation. Consequence is noisy error logs and dependence on exception handling for a routine case; filtered messages should be completed without logging an error.
